findings.claim: The new branch is gated on flag `use-table-widget-visualization`, which is not registered in src/sentry/features/temporary.py. The branch is dead code. If the flag were enabled it would render TableWidgetVisualization with columns={[]} and empty data, ignore tableResults and loading, and show an empty table. This breaches CLAUDE.md 'Feature Flags: Always add for new features'.
findings.evidence: `grep -rn "use-table-widget-visualization" src/` returns nothing, while the patch's other flags are at temporary.py:441 and :278. `grep -rn "table-widget-visualization" src/ static/` matches only chart.tsx:164. Failing check: `grep -q "use-table-widget-visualization" src/sentry/features/temporary.py || echo MISSING` prints MISSING. Severity was Important from mattpocock and ponytail, Minor from open-code-review and superpowers; normalised to Important.
findings.reason: Four seats agree. The red check is the grep command above, which fails on the pinned code. Fix options: register the flag and feed tableResults to the component, or drop the branch (with the :141/:152 organization destructure and rename) until the component has real data. Caveat: whether getsentry registers the flag was not checked (ponytail).

findings.claim: fetch_error_details pairs error_ids with events.values() using zip. It assumes nodestore get_multi returns values in input order with no gaps, so error IDs can be attached to the wrong event's title, message and timestamp.
findings.evidence: nodestore/base.py get_multi dedupes IDs. On a partial cache hit it returns fetched items first and then cached items (items.update(cache_items), base.py:184,199-205). Some backends omit missing IDs. Proposed failing test (open-code-review): store events A and B, warm the cache for A only, call fetch_error_details(project.id,[A,B]), and A's entry gets B's title. open-code-review rated it Important; superpowers rated it Minor and said the ID is not used in log text today, so the impact is latent; mattpocock raised it outside its axis.
findings.reason: Three seats agree. The highest correctness-seat severity, Important, is kept: superpowers' latent-impact remark is reasoning, not a source citation that disproves it. Red test: open-code-review's partial-cache test. Fix: look up events.get(node_id) for each node_id/event_id pair instead of zipping.

findings.claim: The checks that age and timestamp are mutually exclusive test truthiness (self.initial_data.get("age")). A report with age: 0 (the usual value for a fresh report) together with timestamp passes validation.
findings.evidence: Lines 52 and 58 use .get() truthiness. Ponytail notes that a single validate(attrs) checking `"age" in attrs and "timestamp" in attrs` fixes it. Reasoned in all seats; no seat ran it.
findings.reason: Four seats agree. Red test: POST a report with age: 0 and timestamp and expect a validation error. It passes on the pinned code.

findings.claim: age and timestamp are both required=False, so a report with neither field is accepted, although the validators' docstrings say one must be present.
findings.evidence: Reasoned from the serializer field definitions and validator docstrings (mattpocock #8, open-code-review #7, superpowers #6).
findings.reason: Three seats agree. Red test: POST a report with neither age nor timestamp and expect 422. It is accepted on the pinned code.

findings.claim: `enabled: Boolean(normalizedDateRange)` is always true because normalizeDateTimeParams returns an object, so it gates nothing.
findings.evidence: normalizeDateTimeParams returns an object and an object is always truthy (open-code-review #12, ponytail #8, superpowers #12, which cites line 36).
findings.reason: Three seats agree. Minor. Fix: gate on the intended condition or drop the option.

findings.claim: get_environment_info calls issue.get_recommended_event() for each issue in the PR-comment task: a Snuba query plus a nodestore/DB fetch per issue, which is the N+1 anti-pattern in CLAUDE.md.
findings.evidence: Called per issue from github/integration.py:409 and gitlab/integration.py:257. The list is capped by set_limit(5) at commit_context.py:572 and runs inside a task.
findings.reason: Three seats agree, but all rate it Minor and the cost is bounded at 5 issues in an async task. Defer with `ponytail: bounded N+1 (<=5 issues, in task); batch if the limit grows`.

findings.claim: Errors are interleaved with breadcrumbs by comparing nodestore error timestamps (seconds) with rrweb event timestamps (milliseconds). error_ts < event_ts is always true, so every error is emitted before the first breadcrumb and the order is never chronological.
findings.evidence: rrweb fixtures use ms (tests/sentry/replays/unit/test_event_parser.py:329: 1674291701348). The new tests at test_project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py:188 use seconds, which hides the bug. Superpowers EXECUTED a repro, `python3 -I .scratch/repro_replay_ts.py ...`, that fails on HEAD: breadcrumbs at 1700000000000 and 1700000005000 ms with an error at 1700000002.0 s come out with the error first.
findings.reason: Appendix: raised by two seats, so under the agreement split it is not reported or fixed. Flagged for the user: this is the best-evidenced finding in the merge (an executed failing repro from a correctness seat, corroborated by a second correctness seat), and the three-seat threshold excludes it.

findings.claim: destination and attempts are required serializer fields, but per the W3C Reporting spec they are internal to the user agent and absent from real browser POSTs. Real Chrome payloads would get 422 for the whole batch.
findings.evidence: Reasoned from the W3C 'serialize reports' algorithm; no captured payload was checked. Both fixtures (DEPRECATION_REPORT, INTERVENTION_REPORT) invent these fields. Failing test: POST [{"age":0,"type":"deprecation","url":"https://x.com/","user_agent":"UA","body":{}}] with the option enabled and expect 200; it gets 422. Superpowers notes the old dataclass had the same assumption, so this is not a regression.
findings.reason: Appendix: two seats, so not fixed per the agreement split. Unverified: the spec reading has not been checked against a captured browser request.

findings.claim: The HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES filter (is_segment, project_id, received) runs only after the early `if (!searchQuery.trim()) return sorted;`. In the default no-search view the attributes are still shown; they are hidden only while the user searches.
findings.evidence: Reasoned from code order at :61-69. Failing test: render Attributes with an attribute named project_id or is_segment and no search; it is rendered.
findings.reason: Appendix: two seats, so not fixed per the agreement split.

findings.claim: One invalid report in a batch causes the whole batch to be rejected.
validate_timestamp and validate_age mirror each other; one validate(attrs) would replace both. Also, str(browser_report["type"]) at :126 is redundant because ChoiceField already returns a string.
The rewritten tests no longer post content_type="application/reports+json", so the custom BrowserReportsJSONParser has no coverage of a passing request, only the 415 negative test.
findings.evidence: `grep -n "reports+json"` on the test file returns nothing (mattpocock #8).

findings.claim: Under pagination every page gets the replay's full error list via functools.partial(..., error_events). Errors not yet emitted are appended at the end of each page, so they repeat across pages and land in the wrong context.
Node IDs are built with the replay's project_id, so errors from other projects in the replay's error_ids (e.g. a backend project) are silently dropped.
The Snuba replay query runs even when enable_error_context=false.
ErrorEvent.category is always set to "error" and never read; generate_error_log_message uses only title, message and timestamp.

The new feedbackSummary.tsx and useFeedbackSummary.tsx have no colocated .spec.tsx, breaching CLAUDE.md Frontend Rule #5. The hook's tooFewFeedbacks logic and the component's hide/placeholder states are untested.
The pending, error and success branches each build the same return object; one expression would do. The feature flag is checked both here and in feedbackSummary.tsx.
The new hook has no colocated spec. It is exercised only through useTraceItemAttributeKeys.spec.tsx without queryString, so the substringMatch path is untested.
The search/queryString parameter is speculative: the only caller never passes it.
try/catch rethrows as `new Error(`...${e}`)`, which turns the ApiError into a plain string and discards responseJSON.
findings.evidence: Ponytail #5 cites the rethrow at :76-86; superpowers #15 makes the same claim under the useTraceItemAttributeKeys refactor.

findings.claim: When projects is passed, projectIds is a new array every render, so both useMemos recompute every time. Options are also built twice (for queryKey and inside getTraceItemAttributeKeys).
The attribute-keys request no longer sends environment, a behaviour change. A code comment at useGetTraceItemAttributeKeys.tsx:50 says this is intentional.
findings.reason: Appendix: two seats. Marked intentional in the code; needs author confirmation.

findings.claim: The refactor drops staleTime: 0 and retry: false in favour of queryClient defaults, and isLoading now reflects isFetching, so it is true during background refetches.
